fields.bmcage\n\n 2013-06-23 09:48\n\ndeveloper:
Question is, is this correct behavior?

I understand that group name is used in Slavic countries for female/male variants of the same name, it was added to Gramps years ago by a Russian in America.
However, group name in essence can be used for other things, as it mainly is a display issue: grouping people in the tree person view.

Hence, I'm afraid if we do this, we obtain a bug ticket soon after that people with different names but same group names are counted as same name.

How to fix that?

for quick views, you can make a base quick view, and then derive two different quickviews: Same Surnames, and Same Group Names. Same for FilterByName quickview. Difference is only in what surname is used

for the gramplets, an option can be added to the settings, so as to indicate group names must be used, not surnames. I'm ok if that preference setting is by default set to True.

As to the code:
if group_as and group_as != "":

better:

if group_as and group_as.strip() != "":

same for global_group_as line.
fields.aglebov\n\n 2013-06-23 10:20\n\ndevelope:
There seems to be another problem: local overrides (i.e. when the user clicks "Group this name only") are already counted as one name, whereas global ones ("Group All") are not.
But yes, backward compatibility is always an issue.
fields.bmcage\n\n 2013-06-23 10:41\n\ndeveloper:
It is not so much backward compatibility, but culture differences. Slavic Kacur and Kacurova can be counted together, but if people use group name to group spelling variants over time, they might still want to run reports/gramplets based on the actual name in the source.

So, as to move forward, can you extend your patches as requested?
fields.aglebov\n\n 2013-06-23 10:55\n\ndevelope: The suggestions seem to complicate things rather than simplify them.

 global-surnames-mapping-3.patch (5,673 bytes)
and finally a print statement is removed in the third patch

Question is, is this correct behavior?

I understand that group name is used in Slavic countries for female/male variants of the same name, it was added to Gramps years ago by a Russian in America.
However, group name in essence can be used for other things, as it mainly is a display issue: grouping people in the tree person view.

Hence, I'm afraid if we do this, we obtain a bug ticket soon after that people with different names but same group names are counted as same name.

How to fix that?

for quick views, you can make a base quick view, and then derive two different quickviews: Same Surnames, and Same Group Names. Same for FilterByName quickview. Difference is only in what surname is used

for the gramplets, an option can be added to the settings, so as to indicate group names must be used, not surnames. I'm ok if that preference setting is by default set to True.

As to the code:
if group_as and group_as != "":

better:

if group_as and group_as.strip() != "":

same for global_group_as line.

There seems to be another problem: local overrides (i.e. when the user clicks "Group this name only") are already counted as one name, whereas global ones ("Group All") are not.
But yes, backward compatibility is always an issue.

It is not so much backward compatibility, but culture differences. Slavic Kacur and Kacurova can be counted together, but if people use group name to group spelling variants over time, they might still want to run reports/gramplets based on the actual name in the source.

So, as to move forward, can you extend your patches as requested?
The suggestions seem to complicate things rather than simplify them.
Covering all bases always is more complex
